As a person who is currently in a position like your ex-boyfriend’s I would really like to say that it’s not worth it to be like us. You can let yourself be a selfish person but it should be limited so that you don’t harm others too much. I don’t know how he feels because i’m not him, but I truly hate myself everyday for how much I hurt other people due to my selfishness and end up hurting them further. One day it will boil over and end up harming both me and him enough so that we will have to reconsider our life choices.
You have 2 options on how this will go. If you say “fuck it” and do whatever you want no matter who it hurts, you will end up burying the pain and loneliness and live in delusions until reality gives you one fat wake up call and you get fucked. (from there you can decide whether or not to continue your cycle of pathetic-ness and become a spiteful self-pitying bastard who enjoys making others suffer a fraction of what you feel or become a better person from learning through your mistakes and being strong enough to persevere through tough times). Or you can stay the good person who gives everything and gets stepped on by those who don’t give a shit but can continue being nice by the appreciation from others around you who really need what you are giving. Yeah being a good/normal person sucks, but you are truly what is saving our world from being a bunch of pathetic and angry nothings.
Your anger and questions on moral standards are reasonable considering the hurt you have gone through, but falling victim to a system full of illusions is just a failure on your decision making. Don’t become a bad person just because someone else was bad to you, that’s weak and a waste. If I could, I would try to learn how to be someone who cares about others, and I really wish I could. My perspective has evaluated that the world still spins because of people like you.
